m_de0d792ea7b8: I've set up my Mac so that it is as fast to navigate through and work on as Linux. The main things I did this with are:
m_13995b43eb5d: Starting with the simplest one, Rectangle is just my window manager. I really only ever use the binding <s0>left_option + left_control + enter</s0> for full-screening and centering a window.
m_2dc4bd3b88ac: <s0>The key to all of this is never ever use the desktops or built in full screen of macOS. This will massively slow down your jumping between apps, just fullscreen them and jump around with <s1>cmd + tab</s1> and the Raycast opening shortcuts.</s0>
m_a509d53ea080: The next key piece is Karabiner Elements. I use this to make a <s0>hyper key</s0> on caps lock. I have it bound so that if you tap it, it presses escape, and if you press it with something else it acts as <s1>control + option + shift + command</s1>. This is insanely powerful for navigation and work, especially when combined with Raycast.
m_bb21ef90524b: I have Raycast bound to <s0>hyper + space</s0> (which is really <s1>caps lock + space</s1>). Then in Raycast if you search extensions, then search for an application, then you can set a keybinding for it. Mine are all hyper + something. You can see them all <s2>here</s2>.
m_0e50bfbb7282: When I setup my Mac I did a ton of custom stuff for tmux, Ghostty, and Cursor. I never read any of the configs for any of them, I just ended up making little commands for OpenCode, then had an AI write them for me. They're not complex, but if you want mine for a reference:
m_0b6c708f814f: Just drop these in and then start OpenCode in the root directory and you can do <s0>/tmux</s0> to customize your tmux config without having to deal with figuring out yet another config setup.
